key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae sacrificial scavenging substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a scalable, low-toxicity route to improve photocatalytic carbon utilization by tuning catalyst composition and pairing it with a carbon-negative biological co-reagent.
method: Designed AB2O6-type HEO (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6 with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to increase surface basicity, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta octahedra for charge transport.
Compared CO2 photoconversion using the HEO alone, with microplastics, and with microalgae as sacrificial agents.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical implementation will need verification of long-term stability, light-to-fuel efficiency, and whether microalgae supply/handling remains feasible at scale.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
